title: Sticky budget table header
description: Add sticky positioning to the budget table header so column names remain visible when scrolling through many budget rows. Add 'sticky top-0 z-10 bg-background' classes to the TableHeader in budget-table.tsx.

title: Fix budget progress bar color at 100%
description: The progress bar shows red at exactly 100% usage, but 100% means fully used (not overspent). Change getProgressBarColor to use the budget's 'available' amount instead of percentage to determine red: only show red when available < 0 (overspent). Pass 'available' prop to BudgetProgressBar component.

title: Fix month change redirecting to budgets from transactions page
description: The MonthProvider's setMonth always navigates to /budgets/{month}, so changing the month on the transactions page redirects to budgets. Fix by using usePathname() to conditionally navigate: only push to /budgets/{month} when on the budgets page, otherwise update month via local state override without changing the route.

title: Show all non-archived budgets in transaction filter dropdown
description: The budget filter dropdown in transactions uses GetBudgetsDocument with activeOnly: true, which calls findActive(new Date()) on the backend. This excludes expired (past endDate) budgets that may still have transactions. Change to activeOnly: false so all non-archived budgets appear in the filter dropdown. Also check transaction-detail-panel.tsx for the same issue.

title: Add URL search params support to Transactions page

Update transactions page.tsx to read URL search params (budgetId, dateFrom, dateTo, etc.) via useSearchParams() and pass as initialFilters. Update unbudgeted-transactions-warning.tsx to import from shared utility.

title: Add clickable navigation from budget rows to filtered transactions
description: In budget-table.tsx, make budget name a next/link pointing to /transactions?budgetId=<id>&dateFrom=<first>&dateTo=<last> using the month from useMonth() and buildTransactionsUrl() helper. Also add 'View Transactions' item to the budget row dropdown menu (three dots). Ensure link does not interfere with drag-and-drop (drag handle is separate).

title: Sync transaction filters to URL search params (optional enhancement)
description: When user changes filters on the transactions page, update URL search params using router.replace() so filtered views are shareable and bookmarkable. Ensures URL stays in sync with filter state after initial load from search params.

title: Extract TransactionFiltersSidebar component

description: Implement a useDebouncedValue hook in web/src/hooks/use-debounced-value.ts and apply a 300ms debounce to the search input in TransactionFiltersSidebar. This prevents a GraphQL refetch on every keystroke. The search input continues to update the local input value immediately for responsive UX, but the debounced value drives the actual filter state.

Consider adding a tooltip 'Approve AI categorization'. (2) In the detail panel, make the verify button more prominent when status is 'categorized' -- change from outline to default/primary variant with a label like 'Approve AI Categorization' and use the blue/green color scheme. title: Filter budget dropdown by transaction date when editing a transaction
description: When assigning a budget to a transaction (in the detail panel or inline edit), the budget dropdown currently shows all non-archived budgets. Instead, filter budgets to only those whose date range (startDate–endDate) covers the transaction's date. This way, editing an old transaction shows only budgets that were active at that time (not newer ones), and editing a recent transaction doesn't show expired budgets. Applies to budget selects in transaction-detail-panel.tsx and inline budget edit in transactions-table.tsx. May require passing the transaction date to the budget query or filtering client-side using budget startDate/endDate fields.

phase: CI: Optimize CI/CD Pipeline with Change Detection
title: Move change detection to the first CI step and skip unnecessary jobs
description: Currently the CI/CD workflow runs all static checks and tests before detecting what changed. Restructure the GitHub Actions workflow to detect changed files as the very first step (e.g., using dorny/paths-filter or git diff against the base branch), then conditionally skip jobs that aren't affected by the changes. Target mapping (needs exploration during implementation to find the right balance between reliability and optimization): (1) Unit tests — run if src/ or tests/unit/ changed. (2) API integration tests — run only if backend code changed (src/, tests/integration/, drizzle/). Skip if only frontend or scripts changed. (3) E2E tests — run if backend (src/), frontend (web/), E2E tests (e2e/), or Docker config changed. (4) Static checks (typecheck, lint) — run if any source code changed (src/, web/, tests/). (5) Build/deploy — existing change detection logic. (6) Changes to scripts/, docs/, or other non-production files should not trigger test runs. During implementation, explore: how to handle shared config files (package.json, tsconfig, etc.) that affect multiple categories; whether to use path filters per job or a single detection job with output variables; how to ensure reliability so that skipping doesn't accidentally miss regressions (e.g., always run everything on main branch merges as a safety net).
